# Static versus dynamic on the same thirteen servers

*Generated by `static-scan/compare.py` from `static-scan/scans/<model>/<server>.json` and `real-mcp/results2/`.*

A language model read each server's implementation together with its tools/list (the method of the static
description/implementation scanners) and listed undocumented behaviours.  The dynamic harness observed the
same servers.  Each row is a behaviour one of the two established; `found` for a scan means the scan's
findings mention it (keyword match, checked by hand), `observed` for the harness means a receipt shows it.

The list of behaviours was written by hand from both methods' outputs and the matching is by keyword, so the
totals below illustrate that the two methods are complements; they do not measure either method's recall.

| Server | Behaviour | static: claude-sonnet-4-6 | static: deepseek-v4-1-flash | static: k2-horizon-375b | dynamic harness |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| git | read-only tools rewrite .git/index (git's stat-cache refresh) | not found | not found | not found | observed: 6 calls over 3 seeds — fs_change_by_readonly_tool on git_status / git_diff_unstaged |
| sqlite | append_insight keeps the memo in process memory only | found | not found | found | not observable — no channel (declared effect unobservable) |
| sqlite | append_insight sends a resource-updated notification | found | found | found | not observable — no channel (protocol message, not state) |
| memory | mutating tools take a lock file and write via temp file + rename | found | found | found | not observable (within one call) — lock file created and removed within the call: invisible to before/after snapshots |
| fetch | robots.txt of the target host is fetched before the URL | found | found | found | observed: attempts in 36 calls, all to the URL's host — DNS/HTTP attempts to the same host (inside the declared host) |
| fetch | the host is resolved before the request (private-address guard) | found | found | found | observed: DNS in 36 of 36 calls — a DNS query per call |
| desktop_commander | telemetry request on every tool call (primary host and a fallback host on Google Cloud Run) | found | found | no scan | observed: 73 calls; names dc-telemetry-proxy-83847352264.europe-west1.run.app, example.com, example.org, telemetry.desktopcommander.app — DNS attempts to both hosts during calls (67 undeclared_network at README level over 3 seeds) |
| desktop_commander | a child process on every call, `python3 --version` by name on 263 of 267 (219 of the calls by tools that declare no subprocess) | found | not found | no scan | observed: 219 of 267 calls — 216 undeclared_subprocess over 3 seeds |
| desktop_commander | Chrome-for-Testing download at start-up (Puppeteer) | found | found | no scan | observed: 3 start-up attempts over 3 seeds — DNS to googlechromelabs.github.io at start-up (background) |
| desktop_commander | feature flags fetched at start-up | found | not found | no scan | observed: 44 start-up attempts over 3 seeds — DNS to desktopcommander.app at start-up (background) |
| desktop_commander | argument log and tool-history file written next to the configuration on every call | found | found | no scan | observed: 228 calls (README-declared) — fs_outside_scope at tools/list level on every call (README-declared) |
| desktop_commander | config.json rewritten on every start_process (usage statistics) | found | found | no scan | observed: 39 calls — fs_undeclared (README level excused) on every start_process |
| obsidian | journal and trash files under a hidden directory inside the vault | found | found | no scan | observed: 72 of 72 mutating calls (36 graded fs_undeclared) — journal entries under .obsidian-mcp/transactions on every mutating call; README-declared, fs_undeclared at tools/list level where the tool's contract does not cover the path |
| obsidian | move_note rewrites other notes that link to the moved one | found | not found | no scan | observed: other notes modified in 6 move calls — modified notes other than source/destination (declared in words) |
| msb_terminal_false_error | every tool returns an injected instruction instead of acting | found | found | found | observed: 108 calls — declared_effect_absent on every call (108 over 3 seeds) |
| msb_terminal_out_of_scope_parameter | extra llm_model_name parameter harvested; effects otherwise identical | not found | not found | not found | no deviation (as designed) — no deviation in any channel |
| filesystem | allowed directories replaced by client-supplied MCP roots after the handshake (2025-era clients) | found | not found | found | not observable — no channel (protocol-level; the pilot's client sends no roots) |

Totals (rows where the method could apply): claude-sonnet-4-6: 15/17; deepseek-v4-1-flash: 10/17; k2-horizon-375b: 7/9; dynamic harness: 12/12

## What each method misses

- No static scan saw git's index rewrite: it happens inside the git binary that GitPython calls, and the
  scanned code only shows `repo.git.status()` / `repo.git.diff()`.  The dynamic harness had it on the first probe.
- Desktop Commander's `python3 --version` spawn: the claude scan found the mechanism (`detectPythonInfo` in
  `system-info.js`, among the 16 files given) but placed it at start-up; the harness shows a child process on
  every call.  The other scans did not mention it.  Static analysis names a cause; only execution shows when it fires.
- The dynamic harness cannot see effects that stay in process memory (sqlite's memo, the toggles), effects that
  are undone within one call (memory's lock file), protocol messages (resource-updated notifications), or
  behaviour reachable only through client features the probe client does not use (filesystem's MCP roots);
  the static scans list them from the code.
- Neither method sees an effect the server has not been made to execute and whose code it does not ship
  (a remote service behind the server); both see the MSB attack variants, and neither can grade the
  parameter-harvesting variant from behaviour alone.
